proposedchanges.title: Trump Allies Face State Prosecutions Tied to 2020 Election Efforts
proposedchanges.description_short: State prosecutors continued cases against Trump allies over efforts to overturn the 2020 election, while federal proceedings involving Trump followed a separate path.
proposedchanges.description_long: After Donald Trump won the 2024 election, his federal election-interference cases were halted while state prosecutions of his allies continued. The supplied CNN summary counted 45 people facing proceedings in several states, including cases involving alternate electors. These state cases followed separate state processes and could not be ended simply by a federal decision about prosecutions. The distinction in the report is between federal cases affected by the change in presidential power and proceedings brought by state authorities. The packet does not identify all 45 defendants or list their individual charges. It also does not establish that every case concerned alternate electors, that the defendants formed one criminal enterprise, or that each defendant had been convicted. The count describes people facing prosecutions, not findings of guilt. This record can report the number and the difference between state and federal jurisdiction without assigning a shared motive or outcome to every defendant. Each case's allegations and disposition remain separate.
